metadata.title: Acme Health Patient Intake API - controlled system

components.title: patient-intake-api
components.description: Telehealth Patient Intake API consisting of API Gateway HTTP API, Lambda handler, DynamoDB intake table, S3 uploads bucket, and supporting security and evidence infrastructure. The Terraform compliance baseline closes GAP-01 through GAP-05, GAP-07, and GAP-08 under the HIPAA Security Rule.
components.purpose: Collect and store patient intake submissions containing PHI with audit-defensible technical safeguards.

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls implemented by the Terraform security baseline. Each requirement identifies the corresponding HIPAA Security Rule provision, the CGE-P gap it closes, the Terraform resources implementing the safeguard, and signed CI evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-01 (HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv)). Patient-uploaded PHI is encrypted at rest using the Acme Health customer-managed KMS key. The S3 uploads bucket uses aws:kms encryption with aws_kms_key.acme, with bucket-key optimization enabled. The policy gap01_s3_cmk_encryption.rego prevents the baseline from reverting to SSE-S3.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-02 (HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv)). The DynamoDB patient intake table uses server-side encryption with the Acme Health customer-managed KMS key rather than an AWS-owned key. The policy gap02_dynamodb_cmk_encryption.rego verifies the CMK reference.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-03 (HIPAA 164.312(e)(1)). The S3 uploads bucket denies all S3 actions when aws:SecureTransport is false, preventing non-TLS access to PHI. The policy gap03_s3_tls.rego verifies that the uploads bucket has the required TLS enforcement policy attached.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-04 (HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)). S3 versioning is enabled on the patient uploads bucket, allowing prior object versions to be recovered following accidental overwrite or deletion. The policy gap04_s3_versioning.rego verifies versioning on the relevant S3 bucket.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-05 (HIPAA 164.312(e)(1)). The patient intake Lambda function is deployed inside the starter VPC using private subnets and a dedicated security group. The workload uses VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and does not require a public Lambda network interface. The policy gap05_lambda_vpc.rego verifies that the Lambda function has the expected private subnet and security-group configuration.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-07 (HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)). The Lambda execution role is restricted to the permissions required by the patient intake workload: DynamoDB PutItem on the intake table, S3 PutObject on the uploads bucket, and KMS decrypt/data-key operations on the Acme Health CMK. Resource-level scoping replaces the starter service-level wildcard permissions. The policy gap07_lambda_least_privilege.rego verifies resource-level IAM scoping.

links.text: CI evidence bundle signed with Cosign; signature bundle stored alongside the evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Closes GAP-08 (HIPAA 164.312(b)). API Gateway access logging is enabled through the default stage and a dedicated CloudWatch log group. AWS management activity is additionally recorded through the multi-region CloudTrail trail with log-file validation enabled. The policy gap08_api_logging.rego verifies the API Gateway access logging configuration.
